units.title: Independent Gaussian rows and their truncated matrix images
units.reader_note: Open the assumptions and source steps for the exact experiment, matrix maps and adjacent Lean.
units.statement: The coordinate-row vectors of the independent-column Gaussian experiment are jointly independent. Their actual truncated matrix images are measurable and jointly independent in that same experiment.
assumptions: Let \(d,q\in\mathbb N\), \(2q+1<d\), and \(r=q+1\). In particular \(d\ge2\), \(r\ge1\), and \(q=0\) is included.

Write \(\gamma_n=N(0,I_n)\) on real Euclidean \(n\)-space. The outcome space is \(\Omega=(\mathbb R^d)^r\), with the literal column-product probability law \(\mu=\gamma_d^{\otimes r}\). Define \(\Phi_i(\omega)=(\omega_{1,i},\ldots,\omega_{r,i})\in\mathbb R^r\).

The public independence conclusion means factorization for every finite family of Borel row events. The canonical row-law declaration supplies row measurability and Gaussian marginal laws internally; neither law nor independence is a caller-supplied certificate.

For the actual matrix consumer, put \(\theta_i=(i-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(t_i[0]=1\), \(t_i[k]=\sqrt2\cos(k\theta_i)\) for \(1\le k\le q\), and \(L=2r+3\log(1000d)\). Lean uses source indices \(i.val+1\) and \(a.val+1\).

Each \(Y_i\) has the displayed literal formula with its own closed cutoff. At entry \(((a,j),(b,k))\), the value inside the cutoff is \(d^{-1}\Phi_i[a]\Phi_i[b]t_i[j]t_i[k]\). Gaussian coordinates come first in both paired indices.

Matrices use their finite real-entry product measurable structure. Both measurability of all \(Y_i\) and full-family independence are proved outputs. The deterministic features vary with \(i\), so no identical-distribution claim for the matrices is made. No Gram, norm, moment, integrability, tail, \(\tau\), or condition-number premise is added.

steps.title: Expose the full scalar-coordinate product
steps.text: Set up the same actual column experiment and reuse the existing canonical row-law theorem. The Mathlib equality identifying the Euclidean image of a scalar Gaussian product with stdGaussian supplies the full physical-coordinate joint law of each column. Unwrap each Euclidean column and apply the finite product-map theorem across columns.
steps.lean:
classical
  dsimp only
  let Q := Fin (q + 1)
  let I := Fin d
  let D := EuclideanSpace ℝ I
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ Q
  let Ω := Q → D
  let μ : Measure Ω := Measure.pi (fun _ : Q => stdGaussian D)
  let row : I → Ω → E := fun i ω => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun a : Q => ω a i)
  let σ : Measure ℝ := gaussianReal 0 1
  let ν : Measure (Q → I → ℝ) :=
    Measure.pi (fun _ : Q => Measure.pi (fun _ : I => σ))
  let ρ : Measure (I → Q → ℝ) :=
    Measure.pi (fun _ : I => Measure.pi (fun _ : Q => σ))
  change iIndepFun row μ
  have row_law := actual_source_row_marginal_law (d := d) (q := q) hq
  change ∀ i : I, MeasurePreserving (row i) μ (stdGaussian E) at row_law

  -- The full physical-coordinate product law, not merely scalar marginals.
  have column_product :
      Measure.map (WithLp.toLp 2 : (I → ℝ) → D)
        (Measure.pi (fun _ : I => σ)) = stdGaussian D :=
    map_pi_eq_stdGaussian
  have unwrap_column :
      MeasurePreserving (fun x : D => fun i : I => x i)
        (stdGaussian D) (Measure.pi (fun _ : I => σ)) := by
    have hm : Measurable (fun x : D => fun i : I => x i) := by
      dsimp [D]
      fun_prop
    refine ⟨hm, ?_⟩
    rw [← column_product, Measure.map_map hm (by fun_prop)]
    change Measure.map id (Measure.pi (fun _ : I => σ)) = _
    exact Measure.map_id
  have unwrap_columns :
      MeasurePreserving (fun ω : Ω => fun a : Q => fun i : I => ω a i) μ ν :=
    measurePreserving_pi (fun _ : Q => stdGaussian D)
      (fun _ : Q => Measure.pi (fun _ : I => σ)) (fun _ => unwrap_column)

steps.title: Regroup the same coordinate array into physical rows
steps.text: Flatten the finite scalar array, exchange its two index factors, and curry it back with the physical-row index outside. The general product-measure curry rules are specialized using the exact equality of finite and infinite product constructions. Each step is a measurable measure-preserving map on the same sampled array.
steps.lean:
-- Flatten, permute the two finite indices, and regroup the same scalar array.
  have flatten :
      MeasurePreserving (MeasurableEquiv.curry Q I ℝ).symm ν
        (Measure.pi (fun _ : Q × I => σ)) := by
    refine ⟨(MeasurableEquiv.curry Q I ℝ).symm.measurable, ?_⟩
    simpa only [Measure.infinitePi_eq_pi] using
      (Measure.infinitePi_map_curry_symm (fun (_ : Q) (_ : I) => σ))
  have swap :=
    measurePreserving_piCongrLeft (α := fun _ : I × Q => ℝ)
      (fun _ : I × Q => σ) (Equiv.prodComm Q I)
  have regroup :
      MeasurePreserving (MeasurableEquiv.curry I Q ℝ)
        (Measure.pi (fun _ : I × Q => σ)) ρ := by
    refine ⟨(MeasurableEquiv.curry I Q ℝ).measurable, ?_⟩
    simpa only [Measure.infinitePi_eq_pi] using
      (Measure.infinitePi_map_curry (fun (_ : I) (_ : Q) => σ))
  have transpose :
      MeasurePreserving (fun x : Q → I → ℝ => fun i : I => fun a : Q => x a i) ν ρ :=
    regroup.comp (swap.comp flatten)

steps.title: Wrap rows and identify their joint law
steps.text: Wrap each scalar row in Euclidean r-space using the same canonical Gaussian product-image equality. Compose column unwrapping, coordinate regrouping and row wrapping. This gives a measurable exact joint pushforward for the actual row maps. The joint transport is an internal proof step.
steps.lean:
have wrap_rows :
      MeasurePreserving (fun x : I → Q → ℝ => fun i : I => WithLp.toLp 2 (x i))
        ρ (Measure.pi (fun _ : I => stdGaussian E)) :=
    measurePreserving_pi (fun _ : I => Measure.pi (fun _ : Q => σ))
      (fun _ : I => stdGaussian E) (fun _ => ⟨by fun_prop, map_pi_eq_stdGaussian⟩)
  have actual_joint :
      MeasurePreserving (fun ω : Ω => fun i : I => row i ω) μ
        (Measure.pi (fun _ : I => stdGaussian E)) :=
    wrap_rows.comp (transpose.comp unwrap_columns)

steps.title: Read full independence from the joint product law
steps.text: The reused row-law theorem supplies measurability and the exact marginal map equalities. Apply the finite-family independence characterization by joint product pushforward. Combining the genuine joint law with those canonical marginal equalities yields full event factorization for every finite family.
steps.lean:
-- Exact joint product law implies full finite-family independence.
  apply (iIndepFun_iff_map_fun_eq_pi_map (fun i => (row_law i).aemeasurable)).2
  calc
    μ.map (fun ω i => row i ω) = Measure.pi (fun _ : I => stdGaussian E) :=
      actual_joint.map_eq
    _ = Measure.pi (fun i : I => μ.map (row i)) := by
      congr 1
      funext i
      exact (row_law i).map_eq.symm

steps.title: Keep the actual truncated matrices as separate row images
steps.text: Define the literal source features and cutoff. For each fixed i, let F_i map one Euclidean row to its inverse-d scaled, locally truncated outer-product tensor. The actual Y_i equals F_i composed with the actual row map on Omega. Reuse both the new independence producer and the same canonical row-law declaration. This fold contains the complete private statement and setup.
steps.lean:
import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumSourceRowIndependence

noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumSourceRowLaw
open AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumSourceRowIndependence
set_option autoImplicit false

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.Tests.GaussianComplexityFixedSpectrumSourceRowIndependence

private theorem actual_truncated_matrices_measurable_and_independent
    {d q : ℕ} (hq : 2 * q + 1 < d) :
  let D := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (q + 1))
  let Ω := Fin (q + 1) → D
  let μ : Measure Ω := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (q + 1) => stdGaussian D)
  let row : Fin d → Ω → E := fun i ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun a : Fin (q + 1) => ω a i)
  let r : ℝ := ((q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  let L : ℝ := 2 * r + 3 * Real.log (1000 * (d : ℝ))
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i =>
    (((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - (1 / 2 : ℝ)) * Real.pi) / (d : ℝ)
  let t : Fin d → Fin (q + 1) → ℝ := fun i k =>
    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * θ i)
  let Y : Fin d → Ω →
      ((Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) → (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) → ℝ) := fun i ω =>
    if ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (fun a => row i ω a) (fun a => row i ω a))
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))
    else 0
  (∀ i : Fin d, Measurable (Y i)) ∧ iIndepFun Y μ := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let Q := Fin (q + 1)
  let I := Fin d
  let D := EuclideanSpace ℝ I
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ Q
  let Ω := Q → D
  let μ : Measure Ω := Measure.pi (fun _ : Q => stdGaussian D)
  let row : I → Ω → E := fun i ω => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun a : Q => ω a i)
  let r : ℝ := ((q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  let L : ℝ := 2 * r + 3 * Real.log (1000 * (d : ℝ))
  let θ : I → ℝ := fun i =>
    (((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - (1 / 2 : ℝ)) * Real.pi) / (d : ℝ)
  let t : I → Q → ℝ := fun i k =>
    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * θ i)
  let F : I → E → ((Q × Q) → (Q × Q) → ℝ) := fun i x =>
    if ‖x‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (fun a => x a) (fun a => x a))
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))
    else 0
  let Y : I → Ω → ((Q × Q) → (Q × Q) → ℝ) := fun i ω => F i (row i ω)
  change (∀ i : I, Measurable (Y i)) ∧ iIndepFun Y μ
  have row_law := actual_source_row_marginal_law (d := d) (q := q) hq
  change ∀ i : I, MeasurePreserving (row i) μ (stdGaussian E) at row_law
  have row_independent := actual_source_rows_independent (d := d) (q := q) hq
  change iIndepFun row μ at row_independent

steps.title: Prove measurable images and preserve independence
steps.text: The squared-norm cutoff is a measurable closed event. Inside it, each matrix entry is a polynomial in two row coordinates with fixed scalar coefficients; outside it, the entry is zero. Thus each F_i is measurable into the finite real-entry product space. Compose with row measurability, then apply full-family independence preservation under the separate measurable F_i. The rule requires no injectivity, and the F_i may differ.
steps.formula: F_i(x)_{(a,j),(b,k)}=\frac{x_ax_b\,t_i[j]t_i[k]}d\mathbf1_{\{\|x\|^2\le L\}},\qquad\forall i,\ Y_i\text{ is measurable};\qquad (Y_i)_{i=1}^d\text{ is independent under }\mu.
steps.lean:
have coordinate (a : Q) : Measurable (fun x : E => x a) := by
    dsimp [E]
    fun_prop
  have cutoff : MeasurableSet {x : E | ‖x‖ ^ 2 ≤ L} :=
    measurableSet_le (by fun_prop) measurable_const
  have F_measurable (i : I) : Measurable (F i) := by
    apply Measurable.ite cutoff
    · apply measurable_pi_lambda
      intro u
      apply measurable_pi_lambda
      intro v
      change Measurable (fun x : E =>
        (d : ℝ)⁻¹ * ((x u.1 * x v.1) * (t i u.2 * t i v.2)))
      exact measurable_const.mul (((coordinate u.1).mul (coordinate v.1)).mul measurable_const)
    · exact measurable_const
  constructor
  · intro i
    exact (F_measurable i).comp (row_law i).measurable
  · exact row_independent.comp F F_measurable

end AutoSamplingTheory.Tests.GaussianComplexityFixedSpectrumSourceRowIndependence

units.dependency_notes: The producer materially reuses the same existing compiled row-law node. The actual private consumer uses this new independence producer and that same row-law node. Canonical Gaussian/product/map facts remain shared Mathlib calls; no duplicate row-law theorem or separate public matrix-consumer credit is introduced.
units.lean_statement: The literal physical coordinate-row family is iIndepFun under the fixed independent-column Gaussian product law.
units.lean_proof: Unwrap the full joint Gaussian coordinate law, flatten/swap/regroup the finite array, wrap rows, and use the joint-product characterization of independence. The actual consumer proves each local truncated matrix image measurable and transports full independence through it.
units.boundary: This local result proves full row-family independence in the canonical independent-column realization and the complete private consumer proves measurability and independence of the actual source truncated matrices. The producer adds independence to the same existing canonical row-law node; it creates no second marginal-law proof. Arbitrary extended-ambient transfer, original matrix-expectation adapters, public aggregate canonicalization, centered variance, matrix concentration, full Lemma4.4, both main lower bounds and exact oracle/TV/precision/worst-query-cap/expected-cost adapters remain open. Serialized integration, actual desktop/mobile/source-index/globalgraph/copy/download/public delivery and purification remain open.
